sources.rimea: RiMEA e.V., Guideline for Microscopic Evacuation Analysis, version 4.1.1 of 11.09.2025 (German authoritative), https://rimea.de, CC BY-ND 4.0
sources.nist: Ronchi E., Kuligowski E.D., Reneke P.A., Peacock R.D., Nilsson D. (2013) The Process of Verification and Validation of Building Fire Evacuation Models, NIST TN 1822, doi:10.6028/NIST.TN.1822
sources.iso: ISO 20414:2020, Fire safety engineering: verification and validation protocol for building fire evacuation models (paywalled; not read; scope from the ISO page)
sources.percentiles: RiMEA Test 16 percentiles, https://rimea.de/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/test_16_percentiles.xlsx (raw data: Chraibi and Subaih, SingleFileComparator, Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.8378592)

tests.name: speed in a 2 m x 40 m corridor at 1.33 m/s, 0 degrees to the lattice
tests.criterion: time for 40 m within [26, 34] s (expected 30.08 s)
tests.summary: 40 m in 30.08 s (expected 30.08), realised 1.33 m/s, while moving 1.33 m/s

tests.name: speed in a 2 m x 40 m corridor at 1.33 m/s, 45 degrees to the lattice
tests.criterion: time for 40 m within [26, 34] s (expected 30.08 s)
tests.summary: 40 m in 30.08 s (expected 30.08), realised 1.33 m/s, while moving 1.33 m/s

tests.name: speed in a 2 m x 40 m corridor at 1 m/s, 0 degrees to the lattice
tests.criterion: time for 40 m within [38, 42] s (expected 40 s)
tests.summary: 40 m in 40 s (expected 40), realised 1 m/s, while moving 1 m/s

tests.name: speed in a 2 m x 40 m corridor at 1 m/s, 45 degrees to the lattice
tests.criterion: time for 40 m within [38, 42] s (expected 40 s)
tests.summary: 40 m in 40 s (expected 40), realised 1 m/s, while moving 1 m/s

tests.name: speed up a stair 2 m wide, 10 m along the slope
tests.criterion: time for 10 m within Test 1's tolerance scaled, [12.55, 16.42] s, at the model's stair speed 0.689 m/s up (expected 14.52 s)
tests.summary: 10 m in 14.52 s (expected 14.52), moving at 0.689 m/s

tests.name: speed down a stair 2 m wide, 10 m along the slope
tests.criterion: time for 10 m within Test 1's tolerance scaled, [9.42, 12.31] s, at the model's stair speed 0.918 m/s down (expected 10.89 s)
tests.summary: 10 m in 10.89 s (expected 10.89), moving at 0.918 m/s

tests.name: 1 m/s down a stair, 100 m along the incline (10 m run, scaled)
tests.criterion: 100 s for 100 m, within 5 %
tests.summary: 100 m in 100 s, moving at 1 m/s

tests.source: RiMEA 4.1.1 Test 13 (fundamental diagram on stairs: down faster than up)
tests.name: walking speeds down a stair higher than up
tests.criterion: speed down > speed up (and within the spread of Fig. 16)
tests.summary: up 0.689 m/s, down 0.918 m/s (ascent at STAIR_UP 0.75 of kStair)

tests.source: RiMEA 4.1.1 Test 6; NIST TN 1822 Verif.2.3 (IMO Test 6)
tests.name: twenty persons round a corner
tests.criterion: all go round the corner without passing through walls
tests.summary: 100 of 100 out, 0 points of their walks outside the walls
tests.deviation: persons start at random over the whole corridor, not in the 6 m x 2 m start area (crowd.js has no start areas)

tests.source: RiMEA 4.1.1 Test 5; NIST TN 1822 Verif.1.1 (IMO Test 5)
tests.name: pre-movement uniform 10 to 100 s, ten persons in an 8 m x 5 m room
tests.criterion: each starts at an appropriate time: first moves within [10, 100] s, and uniform (KS p > 0.05)
tests.summary: first moves 11 to 99.2 s, KS p 0.775 (crowd.js 'start' is a stagger; the performance check models pre-movement)

tests.source: RiMEA 4.1.1 Test 7; NIST TN 1822 Verif.2.4 (IMO Test 7)
tests.name: 50 persons' unimpeded speeds against the distribution assigned (uniform 0.89 to 1.49 m/s)
tests.criterion: speeds consistent with the distribution assigned (KS p > 0.05)
tests.summary: moving 0.895 to 1.484 m/s (median 1.207) against 0.893 to 1.487; KS p 0.2841
tests.deviation: crowd.js assigns a uniform spread about one speed; RiMEA's population (Weidmann's speeds by age) cannot be set

tests.source: NIST TN 1822 Verif.5.2 (IMO Test 4; MSC/Circ.1238's 1.33 persons/s/m)
tests.name: 100 persons through a 1 m exit: the flow never above 1.33 persons/s
tests.criterion: flow at the exit over the whole period, and in any 10 s, at most 1.33 persons/s
tests.summary: mean 0.923 persons/s, peak 10 s 0.9 (the door's SFPE capacity 0.921)

tests.name: an exit closing at 10 s
tests.criterion: no one steps out by it after it closes; everyone still leaves
tests.summary: 0 steps on to the closed exit begun after 10 s (2 begun before it closed, ending after); 240 of 240 out

tests.source: NIST TN 1822 Verif.3.1 (IMO Test 10); RiMEA 4.1.1 Test 10
tests.name: exit choice in a corridor with twelve rooms, a main and a secondary exit
tests.criterion: a deterministic model sends everyone to the closest exit (NIST); RiMEA's assignment by room cannot be set in crowd.js
tests.summary: nearest: 115 of 115 to their closest exit; 79 of 91 in rooms where RiMEA assigns them; quickest used main 62, secondary 53
tests.deviation: persons start at random over rooms, corridor and passage; RiMEA's per-person exit assignment is not representable

tests.name: room 1's evacuation against the goal's distance a past the bottleneck (0.5 to 10 m)
tests.criterion: the time rises with a until it is constant (documentation)
tests.deviation: about 150 start in room 1 (persons start at random over both rooms; those who start in room 2 are left out of the reading)

tests.name: a 5 m long, 1 m wide bottleneck against a short one
tests.criterion: room 1 takes longer to empty through the long bottleneck
tests.summary: short (one door node) 163.3 s; long corridor 128.8 s; long with door nodes at its ends 167.4 s
tests.deviation: the long bottleneck is two lattice rows (z 5 and 5.5 m); a corridor carries no door capacity in crowd.js, only one person a node

tests.source: RiMEA 4.1.1 Test 12d (Fig. 15, flows from experiments: Kretz et al. 2006; Seyfried et al. 2009; about 1.9 w persons/s)
tests.name: flow through a bottleneck 0.8, 1.0 and 1.2 m wide
tests.criterion: the flow rises with the width (verification); and, as validation, how near it is to the measured flows
tests.summary: 0.8 m: 0.658 persons/s (SFPE 0.658, measured about 1.52); 1 m: 0.921 persons/s (SFPE 0.921, measured about 1.9); 1.2 m: 1.184 persons/s (SFPE 1.184, measured about 2.28)
tests.validation: fails as a match to the measured flows by design: the SFPE capacity is a design value, about half the laboratory flows

tests.source: RiMEA 4.1.1 Test 16 (percentiles: rimea.de test_16_percentiles.xlsx; raw data Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.8378592)
tests.name: single-file fundamental diagram, 200 m corridor one agent wide
tests.criterion: mean speeds between the experiments' 10 and 90 % percentiles at the measured density (validation)
tests.deviation: the lattice holds at most 2 persons/m in single file (0.5 m nodes); measured in x 40 to 80 m between 10 and 40 s, before the exit's queue reaches it

tests.name: fundamental diagram in a 10 m wide corridor (2 m x 2 m measuring area)
tests.criterion: documentation: speed against density beside the model's SFPE relation and Weidmann's
tests.deviation: 100 m long, not 1,000 m; the lattice holds at most 4 persons/m2 (RiMEA asks up to 6); measured between 10 and 40 s

tests.name: 1,000 persons leave a hall by four doors, then by two
tests.criterion: about twice the time with two doors (documentation, not an exclusion criterion: footnote 8)
tests.summary: four doors 274.1 s, two 544.7 s: 1.99 times
tests.deviation: persons spread over the whole hall rather than the 26 m x 16 m area; walking speeds crowd.js's uniform spread, not RiMEA's population

tests.name: 1,000 persons, two exits 5 m apart in one wall
tests.criterion: most prefer the closer exit 1, congestion there, some use exit 2
tests.summary: quickest: 50.2 % by exit 1 (longest wait 527.9 s); nearest: 59.3 %
tests.deviation: persons spread over the whole room, not packed from the left side (crowd.js has no start areas), so exit 2 is the nearer for those far right
